construct: Deficiency or dysfunction of the platelet GPIb-IX-V complex impairs von Willebrand factor-mediated platelet adhesion to damaged subendothelium and produces giant platelets with thrombocytopenia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Mucocutaneous bleeding with giant platelets and thrombocytopenia, despite normal PT/aPTT, identifies Bernard-Soulier syndrome; the causal platelet adhesion defect is loss/dysfunction of the GPIb-IX-V receptor for vWF.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Glanzmann thrombasthenia is a GPIIb/IIIa aggregation defect and does not characteristically produce giant thrombocytopenic platelets. P2Y12, aspirin, and storage-pool defects likewise do not match the receptor-plus-morphology pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Type 2B von Willebrand disease can also cause large platelets and thrombocytopenia, but it is not offered and the lead asks the defining platelet defect of Bernard-Soulier; GPIb-IX-V/vWF binding is unique among the options.
